transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well… I’m here because I need somebody outside the family to understand what’s been going on. It’s my husband’s sister. She’s been working this whole family business—little by little, you know, not in a way everybody wants to admit—to get control of the money and push me out of decisions.

People keep trying to smooth it over like I’m misunderstanding things, or like it’s just normal family tension, but I know what I’ve been seeing. This hasn’t been just one argument or one bad week. It’s been going on for more than a year now, and after a while you start putting the pieces together. I just feel like I’m the only one willing to say what’s actually happening.
Do you believe for certain that your sister-in-law is deliberately trying to take control of the family money and push you out?

Yes. I mean… yes, I do. I know how that sounds when you say it straight like that, but this isn’t me just having a feeling one afternoon or being upset over some little family disagreement.

I came here because my husband’s sister has been working this whole family business in a way that lets her get closer and closer to the money, and at the same time I’m getting pushed out of decisions I should be part of. And everybody keeps trying to make it sound softer, like, “Oh, she didn’t mean it that way,” or “That’s just how families are,” but after more than a year of watching it, I know what I’ve been seeing. It’s deliberate. She knows exactly what she’s doing.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

No… I don’t think so. Not voices like someone talking to me when nobody’s there, no. I mean, sometimes I’ll be thinking things over in my head, going back over conversations, but that’s just me thinking. I’m not hearing some voice in the room or anything like that.
Has your sister-in-law done anything that felt impossible or beyond normal means, like influencing your thoughts or controlling events in a way ordinary people couldn’t?

No, not like… magic or controlling my thoughts, if that’s what you mean. I’m not saying she has some strange power over me or over the house.

What I’m saying is more ordinary than that, but that doesn’t make it less real. She’s been working this family business, bit by bit, getting herself closer to the money and making sure I’m left out of decisions I should be part of. And when I try to point it out, people act like I’m making too much of it, like it’s just a misunderstanding. But I’ve been watching this for over a year now. I know what I’ve been seeing. It’s not beyond normal means—it’s her being deliberate and sneaky.
Have you had a period when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

I don’t think so… not in the way you mean. I’ve had nights where I didn’t sleep well because I was worried or going over things in my head, but that’s not the same as feeling full of energy, you know?

I’m 52, I get tired like anybody else. If I don’t sleep, I usually feel it the next day. I’m not up cleaning the whole house at three in the morning feeling wonderful or anything like that. I can get worked up when I’m upset, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had a period where I suddenly needed hardly any sleep and had all this extra energy.
Apart from your sister-in-law, do you feel that other people are also deliberately trying to harm you or work against you?

No, not really other people, not in the same way. I mean, people may be going along with her, or they may be letting her explain things her way, and that upsets me because it makes me look like I’m the difficult one. But the person I came here about is my husband’s sister.

She’s the one who’s been working this family business, little by little, getting herself in closer to the money and the decisions, and pushing me out like I don’t have a say. And it’s not something that happened once, you know? It’s been over a year of small things, and then when I say something, folks try to smooth it over like, “Oh, that’s just how she is,” or “You’re reading too much into it.” But I know what I’ve been seeing.

So no, I’m not saying everybody is out to get me. I’m saying she is doing this deliberately, and other people just don’t want to admit it.
Have you noticed yourself becoming much less interested in being around people or doing things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in people or stopped doing the things I usually do. I still go to my quilting group, and I still go to choir practice. I’ve been keeping up with my GED lessons too, and I do my senior walks like I normally do. Those things are important to me, and I haven’t just dropped them or anything.

What has changed is more around family, especially anything where my husband’s sister is going to be there. I’m more careful now. I don’t feel comfortable at every gathering the way I used to, because I don’t trust her, and I don’t like sitting there pretending everything is fine when I know what she’s been doing. So I might avoid certain family things, or I might not stay as long, depending on who’s there and what it’s about.

But that’s not me not wanting to be around anybody or not enjoying my life. I still do my regular activities. It’s mostly changed how much I trust her and which family gatherings feel comfortable for me.
Before all this with your sister-in-law began, did you generally tend to distrust other people and suspect they had hidden motives?

I don’t think I was like that before, no. I mean, I’ve never been someone who just trusts everybody right away, but I think that’s normal, isn’t it? You use your judgment. If somebody seems pushy or two-faced, you notice it. But I wasn’t walking around thinking people had hidden motives all the time.

Before this, I got along with people pretty well. I did my things, talked to people, went where I needed to go. I might have had little disagreements here and there, like anyone does, but I wasn’t sitting there studying everybody and thinking they were against me.

This has been different because of how it’s happened and how it keeps happening. So I wouldn’t say I generally distrusted people before. I’d say I was careful, maybe, but not suspicious of everybody.
For how long have you been certain that your sister-in-law is deliberately trying to push you out and take control of the money?

I’d say it’s been about a year and two months now. It started back when the arguments with my husband’s sister began over the family care planning, and that’s when I first really saw what she was doing.

At first, I tried to tell myself maybe it was just a disagreement, maybe she was just being pushy, but over time it became clearer to me. It wasn’t just one argument or one bad day. It’s been going on since then, little by little, and by now I feel certain she’s been trying to push me out and get control over the money side of things.
Do other people ever tell you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?

No, I don’t think people usually tell me that. I mean, sometimes my family might say I’m going on too long about something, but that’s different, I think. I try to explain myself clearly, especially when something matters to me, and maybe I give a lot of background because I don’t want people misunderstanding what I mean.

But I haven’t had people say they can’t follow me, or that I’m jumping all over the place. Not that I can remember. I might circle back to a point if I feel like it didn’t come out right the first time, but in my mind it all connects. So, no, I haven’t really noticed that being a problem.
Have you ever believed that someone was sending you special messages through the television, radio, or internet?

No, not through the television or radio or the internet like that. I don’t think the TV is talking to me or anything.

What I’m saying is more direct than that. I came here because my husband’s sister has been working things in the family business and the money side, trying to get control and push me out of decisions. People try to smooth it over, like, “Oh, she didn’t mean it that way,” or “Don’t make it into something,” but I know what I’ve been seeing. This has been going on for more than a year now, and it’s not some message hidden in a program or online. It’s what she’s doing right in front of everybody, only they don’t want to call it what it is.
